To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the PILPS2e experiment was a success and (2) the PILPS3 experiment was a failure.

1) the PILPS-1b experiment is the most complete and rigorous intercomparison to date of continental surface parameterizations; 2) the experiment is a success because the participating models were forced to run with the same forcing data and because the results were analyzed in a systematic manner; 3) the experiment has revealed that the parameterizations are not consistent with each other; and 4) the experiment has identified the need for further work to improve the parameterizations.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a land surface model for the global climate system.
the development and evaluation of parameterizations of the surface boundary layer for use in general circulation models of the global climate system.

the development and application of models of the land surface and the exchange of heat, water and carbon between the land surface and atmosphere, with the aim of improving our understanding and ability to predict the behaviour of the land surface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PILPS project has been a success in the sense that it has stimulated a number of important research activities, has brought to light a number of important deficiencies in current land surface schemes, and has stimulated the development of new schemes.
PILPS has made a significant contribution in improving the understanding of continental surface processes, and in particular the hydrological cycle, in climate and weather models.
the results of the PILPS Phase 2(a) experiments are not yet sufficient to allow us to make any definitive conclusions regarding the performance of LSMs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to show that the land-surface processes in climate models can have a significant impact on the simulated climate and hydrology.
we are still in a state of infancy in our understanding of the surface-atmosphere interactions and their role in climate change.
we have been successful in developing a new approach to the development of a new model for the development of a model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PILPS2(d) experiment is not a suitable test for the representation of soil moisture dynamics in LSMs.
the PILPS-2e simulations were not able to reproduce the observed spatial patterns and seasonal variations of soil moisture.
there is no single “best” land-surface scheme.
